transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mrs. Hernandez. Hello, Sofia. It is good to see you both again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Buenos días, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it has been a difficult few days since we last spoke. I can see that you are looking quite anxious today. I want to make sure we have plenty of time to go through everything.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Mi hija dice que el doctor tiene respuestas.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sofia, can you tell me what your mother is asking?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She is asking if you have the answers we talked about last time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do have more information. First, I want to be very clear about what happened. As we discussed, there was a mistake with the calendar. Your immunotherapy was given on the wrong day of your cycle. This means the timing of the medicine was not exactly when it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: ¿Qué significa eso para mi cáncer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sofia, could you translate for me?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: She wants to know what this means for her cancer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Because the dose was given on the wrong day, there is a possibility that the treatment won't be as effective as it would have been if it were on the correct day. It is essentially a timing error in the cycle.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Pero usted dijo que era importante el día.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know, Mrs. Hernandez. It is very frustrating and scary when you are counting on these treatments to work and then you find out a mistake was made. I can tell that this is making you feel very uncertain about your progress.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Me siento muy asustada, doctor.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear that fear in your voice. It is completely understandable to feel scared when the plan you trusted was not followed correctly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Who did this? Was it the nurse?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was not the nurse. This was my responsibility. I made the error when I entered the dates into the calendar. I am very sorry. I take full responsibility for this mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did you do that?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I simply entered the date incorrectly. There is no excuse for it. I apologize to both of you for the stress and the worry this has caused your family.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Do we need to change the medicine now? Or do more?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have spent some time reviewing the pharmacology of this specific drug. The immunotherapy works by priming the immune system. Because the window was shifted, we are monitoring how your body responds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you don't know if it worked?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We cannot know for certain until the next scan.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not a good answer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You are right. It is a very unsettling answer. It is difficult to be in a position where we have to wait and see after a mistake has happened. I wish I could give you a definitive yes or no right now, but I cannot.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What happens now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will continue with the rest of the cycle.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When is the next dose? How do we fix the calendar?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on things.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a date. When is the next one?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will check the chart and let you know soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We need to know today. We have to plan the transport.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We will just move forward with the current schedule for now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But will you make the mistake again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will be much more careful. I'll make sure the dates are right.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: How? Do you have a new system?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll just double check it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We need a plan, doctor. My mother cannot keep coming here and wondering if the date is wrong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear how important that certainty is for you and your mother.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Then tell us exactly what happens next.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just continue the treatment as planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which day? Next Tuesday? Wednesday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll send a note to the clinic staff.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are not telling us the date.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have the exact calendar in front of me this second, but we will keep moving forward.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient and daughter to speak fully, never interrupts, and remains regulated despite repeated pushback regarding the schedule.

E.justification: The error is named explicitly and lay language is used, but there are no comprehension checks (e.g., 'Does that make sense?') throughout the transcript.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language ('I am very sorry', 'I apologize'), takes full personal responsibility, and maintains this accountability under questioning.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('anxious', 'frustrating and scary', 'uncertain', 'fear') and engages directly with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The resident provides no specific dates or timelines despite multiple requests and offers only placeholders like 'we will keep an eye on things' and 'I'll send a note'.
